items.name: Readability
items.evidence: normalizeRestoredQueryState relies on many `(resolvedData as any).pages`, `(state as any).failureCount` casts and three-level nested ternaries for fetchFailureReason. The hidden #restoredFromPersister flag and its checks in the observer have no comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The restore logic lives in query.ts, not a separate persister module. The reducer has a side effect: `this.#restoredFromPersister = false` is set inside its cases. queryObserver now depends on query.isRestoredFromPersister(). Vue adapters were changed though the conventions said no adapter changes. normalize is about 70 lines.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: There are defaults via `??`, but no validation of counts or timestamps (NaN or negative values pass through). Loose `as any` / `as unknown as T` casts sit on the restore boundary. `fetchFailureCount ?? (state as any).failureCount` guesses at an alternate field name.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: Symbol marker `persisterRestoreSymbol`, exported from index.ts. fetch() detects it and calls restoreState, so no success callbacks fire. But it goes through the generic setState action, not a dedicated restore action. The bulk path shares normalize but has its own reconcile and build logic.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: createPersister now always returns the restore marker instead of plain data. refetchOnRestore is gated by `!hasPersistedSnapshotMetadata`. shouldFetchOnMount/shouldFetchOptionally skip restored queries, so stale restored data no longer refetches on mount. The public QueryPersister type now includes `PersisterRestoreResult<any, any>`.
